entries.subject: Natural Symmetry Patterns
entries.image_source: native image_gen 1672x941, Pillow Lanczos export to 1920x1080
review_flags: Golden/Fibonacci spiral overlay is schematic; natural spiral/sunflower may not follow exact golden proportions
entries.independent_qa_finding: The sunflower is overlaid with a golden rectangle/Fibonacci-style spiral. In this placement the geometry reads as a measured law of this specimen, whereas the manuscript only describes varied spiral organisation arising for different biological/physical reasons. Natural sunflower phyllotaxis can approximate Fibonacci arrangements; this single overlay does not establish an exact golden spiral.
entries.recommended_follow_up: On a later regenerated candidate, remove the exact-fit overlay or identify it prominently as an illustrative approximation, not a measured fit or universal law. Do not use this image unchanged as evidence for exact golden-ratio organisation.

entries.subject: Mathematical Symmetry and Invariance
entries.image_source: native image_gen 1672x941, Pillow Lanczos export to 1920x1080
review_flags: Finite snowflake is not translationally invariant; clarify translation operator vs group symmetry; inspect D6 equation and reflection notation
entries.independent_qa_finding: The rotation/reflection examples are valid for an ideal regular sixfold shape, and the D₆ example contains only rotation/reflection generators, not translation. The translation panel shows an operation, not an equality claiming the snowflake is translation-invariant; however the overall invariance layout encourages that conflation. The T_(a,b) formula has an unstated active/passive convention, the M_x label is ambiguous for the displayed x-coordinate reversal, and duplicated x/y axis glyphs reduce mathematical legibility. A real finite snowflake is not invariant under translation; it moves to a congruent position.
entries.recommended_follow_up: Regenerate/repair labels: mark the snowflake as idealised; call translation a generic transformation; state that rigid translation preserves shape/area/perimeter but not position/invariance of the finite object; define the translation convention; clarify the reflection axis/subscript and remove duplicate axis glyphs.

entries.subject: Noether's Theorem and Conservation Laws
entries.image_source: native image_gen 1672x941, Pillow Lanczos export to 1920x1080
review_flags: Noether conservation follows continuous symmetry of the action and appropriate system assumptions; imagery depicts angular momentum only
entries.independent_qa_finding: The figure correctly presents one Noether correspondence: continuous rotational invariance → conserved angular momentum, with L = const. It is a schematic, not a derivation. The manuscript caption gives the correct mapping. The visual must not imply angular momentum is conserved for every rotating body regardless of torques.
entries.recommended_follow_up: No image repair required. In any final accessible caption, qualify the conserved quantity as applying when the relevant action/system has continuous rotational symmetry (and, for the mechanical example, with no external torque).

entries.subject: Broken Symmetry and Emergence
entries.image_source: native image_gen 1672x941, Pillow Lanczos export to 1920x1080
review_flags: Two-well 2D potential schematic versus full circular Mexican-hat; assess consistency of narrative and axes
entries.independent_qa_finding: The lower graph is a labelled one-dimensional double-well V(φ) schematic with two degenerate minima, not a circular Mexican-hat surface. The top-to-bottom imagery is conceptual and broadly fits the article’s transition from a symmetric state to lower-symmetry domains. It does not name a specific Higgs mechanism or claim every mass arises by the same mechanism.
entries.recommended_follow_up: No image repair required. Any final caption should explicitly call V(φ) a schematic one-dimensional double-well and avoid naming it a full Mexican-hat potential or universal mass-generation model.

entries.subject: The SYMMETRIA Symmetry Perspective
entries.image_source: native image_gen 1672x941, Pillow Lanczos export to 1920x1080
review_flags: Untested hypothesis caveat absent from image; ensure accessible caption qualifies SYMMETRIA interpretation; verify title not a prohibited decorative masthead
entries.independent_qa_finding: The manuscript caption is explicitly exploratory (‘explores whether’), but that caution is absent in-pixel. Large ‘The SYMMETRIA’ heading reads as a project masthead under the locked gate, despite matching the section’s proper name. The globe-like collage mixes natural forms, Newton’s cradle, a planetary-orbit atom, potential well and abstract geometry; it risks the rejected multi-topic montage and a classical solar-system picture of atoms. No single visual claims a proven unification, but the composition can overstate coherence.
entries.recommended_follow_up: Regenerate as one cinematic, scientifically specific visual for an explicitly exploratory symmetry hypothesis. Use a non-masthead subject title; avoid a planetary atom and unrelated object gallery; label the proposal as untested in the artwork or keep a prominent adjacent accessible qualifier.
